newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end the day sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end the day sharply lower.

text.p: German equities ended the first day's trade of the New Year well down on Thursday in the wake of a slide on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street following stronger-than-expected U.S. manufacturing data.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index slid well over two percent as Wall Street fell early in the New York session following the data in trade which dealers described as low-volume.
The IBIS DAX, which measures electronic trade, closed the day at 2,820.21 points, down 59.26 points or 2.06 percent.

Earlier, the DAX index of floor trade ended down 1.38 percent at 2,848.77 points, while March DAX futures traded 69 points down at 2,835.5 points as German debt futures were taken lower by a fall in U.S. Treasuries.

The dollar, which had provided support to the DAX index earlier on, weakened considerably on the news that the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index had rose to 54.0 in December from 52.7 in November.
Economists had expected the index would decline to 51.5, according to a Reuters poll last Friday.
The weaker dollar hit exporting stocks, especially the chemical companies. BASF AG finished the day down 2.16 marks, or 3.65 percent, at 56.99 marks.
Hoechst AG finished down 2.43 marks, or 3.37 percent, at 69.72 marks and Bayer AG ended IBIS trade down 1.85 marks, or 2.94 percent, at 61.15 marks.

Earlier in the day, the IBIS electronic share dealing system had been delayed by over an hour due to technical problems, but dealers said the lack of any serious trading volumes meant the interruption had had little impact on share values.
"The delay was of little importance because there is scarcely anybody here," one dealer said.
